articles.title: Two Atlanta friends started selling Christmas trees to pay their college fees; a decade later, they have built a seven-location business and donated over $230,000 to help students afford college
articles.summary: Two Atlanta friends, Jack Faught and Calder Johnson, started selling Christmas trees from a pickup truck in 2015 to help pay their college expenses.
articles.body: Two Atlanta friends, Jack Faught and Calder Johnson, started selling Christmas trees from a pickup truck in 2015 to help pay their college expenses. A decade later, their small seasonal venture has grown into a seven-location business that sells thousands of trees during the holiday season and has donated more than $230,000 to community causes. A significant part of the money goes towards college scholarships for students who need help affording higher education. The business has also created seasonal employment opportunities for young people, supported local schools and youth sports programmes, and funded tree-planting initiatives. Their venture has turned a college side hustle into a community-focused enterprise.How two Atlanta friends started selling Christmas treesThe idea took shape in 2015, when Faught and Johnson were 16 and 17 years old and studying at Grady High School, now known as Midtown High School, in Atlanta.The two friends had known each other since first grade and were already working at a Christmas tree lot in Atlanta's Virginia-Highland neighbourhood. While working there, they noticed that customers were paying around $60 for Christmas tree delivery. They saw an opportunity to start their own small business by selling trees and delivering them directly to customers.Johnson had recently acquired a pickup truck, which became their first delivery vehicle. The friends sourced Christmas trees from suppliers outside Atlanta, transported them in the truck and sold them to neighbours. They began by going door to door and delivering trees to customers' homes.Their first season was modest, with approximately 30 trees sold. However, the venture helped them earn money towards their college expenses, including tuition, accommodation, food and other living costs.From a pickup truck to seven Christmas tree locationsAs demand grew, the friends began expanding beyond home deliveries. In 2019, they secured a pop-up location through Inter Atlanta FC, a local football club with which both had previously been associated. They reportedly sold around 500 trees at that location before December began.In 2020, they launched a website and purchased 500 Christmas trees for the season. The entire stock sold out before December, encouraging them to expand further.After graduating from the University of Georgia in 2021, where they studied finance and marketing, the two decided to make the business their full-time occupation. They eventually expanded to seven locations across metro Atlanta.By the 2025 Christmas season, the business was expecting to sell more than 4,000 trees. Its products include Fraser fir Christmas trees, wreaths and garlands, along with delivery, installation and post-holiday collection services.The trees are primarily sourced from Christmas tree farms in North Carolina, while some varieties, including Noble firs, come from Oregon.How the Christmas tree business funds college scholarshipsInitially, the business was meant to help the founders pay for their own education. However, after graduating, they decided to use its profits to support other students.In 2021, they established a scholarship programme for students from Atlanta and surrounding communities. During its first year, six students received scholarships of $2,000 each.The business operates on a seasonal model, with profits from Christmas tree sales supporting scholarships and other community initiatives after operating expenses are covered. These expenses include purchasing trees, paying employees, transportation and running the different locations.According to the founders, 100% of the profits remaining after these expenses are donated to community causes.The organisation's official website reports more than $230,000 in cumulative donations since 2020. Its reported impact includes $120,245 in scholarships awarded to 58 students.Students can apply for scholarships through the programme, with preference given to applicants from Atlanta-area schools. The application also asks them to explain how they intend to make their community or the wider world a better place after college.The business also creates jobs and supports local communitiesBeyond scholarships, Trees for Tuition has created seasonal employment opportunities for high-school and college students. The business has employed more than 100 people, most of them students, according to a 2023 report by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution.It also supports local schools through donations to Parent Teacher Organisations and helps young footballers from families who might otherwise struggle to afford participation in the sport.One of its beneficiaries is Inter Atlanta FC, the football club where the founders played when they were younger. The business contributes towards registration fees, uniforms, equipment and other expenses for young players.In addition, the founders have partnered with tree-planting organisations to support reforestation. Trees for Tuition says it plants one tree for every Christmas tree sold. Its website reports that more than 23,000 trees have been planted through the initiative.The business has also expanded into seasonal pumpkin sales, offering pumpkin delivery and collection services during autumn. These activities allow it to support community projects beyond the Christmas season.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in Germany, Austria and Hungary
articles.summary: Dozens of cases are reported in Austria, Germany and Hungary, including a nine-year-old girl hurting her tongue while eating chocolate containing a pin.
articles.body:
Needles and other sharp metal objects have been found in sweets handed out over Halloween in Germany, Austria and Hungary, prompting police to issue warnings to parents to check what their children have been given.

Police in a number of German states have reported cases, from Bavaria in the south-east to Lower Saxony in the north.

A girl aged nine hurt her tongue while eating a chocolate bar in Bremervörde, west of Hamburg. A 5cm-long (2in) pin was then found inside it.

Meanwhile, police in Hungary have launched a criminal investigation after nails, screws and pieces of wire were found in sweets handed out to children who had been trick-or-treating in and around the town of Gyömrő, to the east of Budapest.

The local authority said one young girl had been handed a toffee with a nail inside a chocolate wrapper and that she had fortunately noticed in time and had not swallowed the sweet.

Several cases have also been reported across Austria, where Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as "cowardly, malicious and in some cases life-threatening".

Police there said investigations were under way in four states, and that a 10-year-old girl had suffered a minor injury to her mouth when she bit into a small chocolate bar in the Amstetten area to the east of Linz.

Lower Austria Governor Johanna Mikl-Leitner said the perpetrators had to feel the full force of the law, adding: "Our children deserve a carefree childhood and we'll continue to ensure that."

Warning after 'metal pins' found in Halloween sweets

German police in the south-eastern state of Bavaria said that, while there had been similar cases reported in the past two years, initial figures this year suggested a significant increase in incidents.

As many as 25 cases involving sweets containing needles, screws or nails have been reported by police in Bavaria.

Police in the Middle Franconia region of western Bavaria have also warned of the risk of copycat actions, after a mother found a needle in her child's chocolate bar and reported it to police.

She later returned to the police to say her child had admitted to inserting the needle.

articles.title: UK Supreme Court hears appeal against Palestine Action’s proscription
articles.summary: Rights activists say UK decision against Palestine Action is a ‘misuse of terrorism powers’.
articles.body:
An appeal challenging the designation of Palestine Action as a “terrorist” organisation has begun at the United Kingdom’s top court, as police arrested demonstrators who gathered outside to protest against the group’s proscription.

The two-day hearing at the Supreme Court in London began on Wednesday. Huda Ammori, cofounder of Palestine Action, said ahead of the hearing that she would argue the ban is having a disproportionate effect on freedom of speech and the right to protest.

The direct action group was proscribed by the UK government under then-Prime Minister Keir Starmer in July last year. The decision has since been denounced by rights groups, including Amnesty International and Liberty.

Palestine Action describes itself as a “direct action movement committed to ending global participation in Israel’s genocidal and apartheid regime”. Its designation as a “terrorist” organisation puts it on the same list as armed groups such as al-Qaeda and ISIL (ISIS). Those found guilty of belonging to or supporting Palestine Action risk up to 14 years in prison.

As the hearing got under way, protesters gathered outside the court. Some expressed support for Palestine Action, while others opposed the group’s proscription, which many view as an affront to civil liberties. One demonstrator held a placard reading: “God help us Jews who support Palestine and Palestine Action”.

About 25 protesters were arrested, according to the Press Association; the final person detained carried a sign saying: “God help us who are not married to the UK’s national security adviser who support Palestine and Palestine action.”

It’s understood this is in reference to journalist and author Sarah Helm, who is married to the UK Prime Minister’s national security adviser, and who had earlier posted a similar line on X but did not face prosecution.

“Today was another demonstration of the chaos wrought by the Government’s grave misuse of terrorism powers to proscribe Palestine Action,” Tom Southerden, Amnesty International’s UK Law and Human Rights Director, said in a statement issued after Wednesday’s arrests.

“The sight of musicians, politicians and celebrities being arrested for peacefully holding placards is a grim one. That they were arrested for using the same language that Sarah Helm didn’t face arrest for, shows how dangerously vague our terrorism laws are.”

Amnesty is one of several organisations calling for the UK government to lift the ban on Palestine Action.

“Whatever the Supreme Court ultimately decides, it’s long past time for the Government to admit they got this badly wrong, end the proscription of Palestine Action and put a stop to these appalling arrests,” Southerden said.

The UK government’s crackdown on pro-Palestine voices has come under intense scrutiny since Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza more than three years ago.

Last week, Swedish academic Andreas Malm was prevented from entering the UK after the government said his presence was “not conducive to the public good”. Malm is a vocal supporter of Palestine and has spoken out against Israel’s assault on Gaza.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said before taking office in July that the Labour Party had “got it wrong” on Gaza. However, his comments have come under renewed scrutiny after Malm was refused entry to the UK last week.

articles.title: Chloe Mitchell: Brandon Rainey in court accused of 2023 murder
articles.summary: Brandon Rainey of James Street, Ballymena denies the murder of the 21-year-old in Ballymena in 2023.
articles.body:
The man accused of killing Chloe Mitchell murdered her at his house before dismembering her body and disposing of it in wheelie bins, a court has been told.

Brandon Rainey, formerly of James Street, Ballymena, denies murdering the 21-year-old in June 2023 and preventing the lawful burial of her remains.

At Belfast Crown Court on Wednesday morning the prosecution opened its case against Rainey.

Crown barrister David Russell KC told the jury it was the prosecution's case that Chloe Mitchell and Rainey had been in "an on-off relationship" and that he killed her in the early hours of 3 June, sometime between 00:36 and 05:18 BST.

"We say a wealth of evidence will show beyond reasonable doubt that the accused murdered her and disposed of her body in a way that prevented her burial," Russell said.

Jurors were told Chloe Mitchell had significant addiction issues and was last seen alive by two of her friends in the company of Rainey in his flat in James Street shortly before her death.

The court also heard that one of her friends later told police that Rainey had made a comment while they were at his flat that he would "love to chop someone up and melt them in the bath" but then claimed he was joking.

When Chloe Mitchell was discovered to be missing, one of those friends contacted Rainey, who told her she had only stayed about 15 minutes and left after an argument "to go to Belfast to see some fella," the court was told.

Extensive searches were launched by police to try to find Chloe Mitchell.

Her dismembered remains were found by a police officer on 11 June in two bins in James Street.

A post-mortem examination of her remains concluded that she had died as a result of blunt force trauma to the head, possible gagging, and stab wounds to the chest.

Forensic investigations of Rainey's flat found Chloe Mitchell's blood in several areas of the property.

The prosecution said when Rainey was arrested and interviewed by police he denied any involvement in Chloe Mitchell's death or the disposal of her body.

Russell said he had "lied repeatedly and in a determined fashion" to investigating officers.

Rainey sat in the dock in a grey tracksuit throughout the proceedings.

David Russell KC told the court Chloe Mitchell had suffered "a cruel and brutal death" at Rainey's hands.

"She had been the victim of a sustained assault with weapons whilst alive and then mutilated and dismembered in death," he said.

"We say when you stand back and hear all the evidence in this case you will be satisfied beyond reasonable doubt that Brandon Rainey murdered Chloe Mitchell."

articles.title: Javits Frimpong: Mother flies from Ghana to the US to seek justice
articles.summary: Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys.
articles.body:
The mother of a 15-year-old Ghanaian boy who was fatally shot in the United States last week has left Ghana for America after being granted an emergency visa by President Donald Trump.

"I want justice for my son," Doris Adu Gyamfi told the BBC at the airport before her departure.

She said he had dreamt of becoming a medical doctor.

Her son, Javits Frimpong, who had only been in the US for a year, was chased down and shot on Thursday morning on his way to school in the Bronx, New York.

He was taken to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys in connection with the shooting.

His death has sparked outrage in both Ghana and the US, and reignited the debate about gun violence in America.

His mother was escorted to the airport by relatives and Dr Erieka Bennett, Head of Mission of the African Diaspora Forum.

"I'm going to America to plan my son's funeral," Gyamfi said.

She thanked the government and well-wishers for their support and prayers following her son's death.

In a social media post on Saturday, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani said Trump had agreed to grant a visa to Gyamfi so she could mourn her son in person.

Mamdani said the murder of a child was a pain no parent should endure, "let alone from thousands of miles away.”

"Javits Frimpong's mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately," he said.

"All of New York City is mourning this tragedy," he added.

Ghana's government has condemned the killing and said it was following the case closely to ensure justice.

It has urged US authorities to conduct a thorough investigation and said it was ready to provide legal and consular support to ensure the perpetrators are brought to justice.

Police are searching for three teenage suspects who fled the scene, captured on surveillance footage.

The shooting has sparked concern among Ghanaians about the safety of children sent to study in America.

articles.title: PSNI pays undisclosed sum to relatives of 1992 UVF murders
articles.summary: Relatives of Charles and Teresa Fox and Kevin McKearney sued the police over the alleged involvement of state agents.
articles.body:
The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) has paid undisclosed damages in connection with loyalist shootings in County Tyrone which left four Catholics dead.

Relatives of Charles and Teresa Fox and Kevin McKearney sued the police over the alleged involvement of state agents.

Along with John McKearney, they were murdered by the Ulster Volunteer Force (UVF) in two separate attacks carried out in Moy in 1992.

Kevin McKearney's widow, Bernie, said the settlement is "nice", but added: "Nobody is ever going to be held accountable.

"I feel we are never going to get justice."

Their solicitor, Gavin Booth, said the damages are "significant".

The High Court in Belfast heard the settlement followed negotiations and that the families were "relieved" the civil case is over.

Addressing the court, Mr Justice Rooney said he hoped the settlement would provide "some closure".

Stating that four innocent victims had been brutally murdered, he added: "I can't imagine the pain and suffering you have gone through."

He said the cases had been "close to my heart".

The government has previously rejected calls for a public inquiry into the murders - despite a coroner suggesting it is the best way forward.

Their inquests were stopped two years ago after sensitive intelligence information was not disclosed.

Kevin McKearney, a father of four, was working behind the counter of the butcher shop on 3 January 1992 when a gunman walked in and shot him several times.

His 68-year-old uncle John - known as Jack - was shot and seriously wounded in the attack.

He died from his injuries three months later on 4 April 1992.

On 6 September 1992, Charles and Teresa Fox, aged 63 and 54 respectively, who had a family of six children, were shot dead in their home.

Their bodies were discovered by two of their children the morning after the attack.

The couple were the parents-in-law of Kevin McKearney.

Speaking outside the High Court, relatives said the settlement is not the end of the matter.

They want to know the details of the withheld intelligence.

However, Patricia Kearney, one of the Fox children, said: "There is a lot of information we will probably never get in our lifetime.

"If it was released it would be damaging and that's the way it has always been."

The families also sued the Ministry of Defence (MoD), but the court was told that action has now been discontinued.

Booth added: "To date we have had no inquest or no gist (of the intelligence) which stopped the inquest.

"While today is a step forward, we call on the Secretary of State to give them their inquest, or give them a public inquiry."

articles.title: Time to focus on cost of living, says PM after US election results
articles.summary: Andy Burnham says prices won't come down until the US's conflict with Iran is resolved.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has said the results of the US midterm elections meant there was an "opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living".

Speaking to broadcasters from the Commonwealth leaders summit, the prime minister promised to push for a resolution to the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine in the wake of the US elections that saw Donald Trump's Republicans suffer heavy losses.

He said he couldn't ease cost of living pressures until the US's conflict in Iran had been resolved.

Responding to the midterm results, the US president acknowledged that rising fuel prices - caused by the Iran war - had played a part in his party's defeats.

Speaking to Fox News, President Trump said: "People agree with what I'm doing on Iran but they really probably weren't willing to do the short term consequences of paying more for gasoline - I understand that."

Giving his reaction to the results, Burnham said the voters in the US have said they want to "see the world coming together and focusing on the things that matter to people".

Asked whether he thought the results might make the US president more unpredictable, Burnham said: "President Trump has accepted the results, and I feel the world has an opportunity now to unite around the issue that is affecting us all, and that's the cost of living.

"That has been the issue that I have put front and centre in my first three months in Downing Street, and we've made moves.

"But I can't get people's cost of living pressures down until the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, the conflict in Ukraine started by Russia.

"These are the things we have to focus on now, and I hope the world has a moment to do that.

"And certainly, in my calls with leaders, that is what I will be asking everybody to do."

Five reasons why Republicans lost so badly

Everything you need to know from the US midterm elections

The subject of the US midterm elections was raised at Prime Minister's Questions, which, in Burnham's absence, was taken by Cabinet Office Minister Louise Haigh.

The Liberal Democrat's deputy leader Daisy Cooper said American voters had rejected Trump's "warmongering and the economic chaos that it has caused".

She expressed concern that the US president was planning further strikes on Iran and urged the government to "stand together with our reliable allies and send a clear message to Trump and Netanyahu: there must be no more strikes."

Haigh replied: "The US are one of our most important allies and our priority absolutely is de-escalation."

She said the Iran war had been "catastrophic for the cost of living crisis" and said the Conservatives and Reform should "consider very carefully their judgment in calling for us to jump so readily into it".

Asked about suggestions there could be an attack on Iran in the coming week, Trump told the Financial Times on Tuesday: "The US was "locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no need for it".

Indirect talks between the two sides have been stalled for months and some analysts close to the Iran regime have suggested prolonging the negotiations, in the hope that the rising cost of fuel would damage Trump electorally.

Although the US Congress, now controlled by the Democrats, can restrict funding, Trump will still have significant authority over foreign policy.

Burnham is preparing a 10-year plan for government, and will be hoping that his strategy isn't blown off course by the actions of an unpredictable US president in his last two years in the White House.

articles.title: At Blenheim Palace, a Roman sarcophagus served as a water feature and garden container for nearly a century; experts identified it as 1,700 years old and moved it indoors
articles.summary: A 1,700-year-old Roman sarcophagus repurposed as a flowerpot was recently identified at Blenheim Palace. Experts moved the remarkable artifact indoors after its rediscovery, highlighting its connection to ancient mythology and Roman burial customs.
articles.body: A container holding tulips in the grounds of Blenheim Palace had spent nearly two centuries away from its original purpose. According to the BBC, its carved marble front had a direct link to a Roman sarcophagus made around 300 AD. The object had been repurposed at first as a water feature and later used as a garden container. When an antique specialist, during an unrelated visit, stumbled upon the relic, its identity came to light after he recognised it. Over the following months, its removal, conservation and transfer to an indoor display were orchestrated.The mythology carved into the marble The container’s panel depicts Dionysus, the Greek god associated with wine and festivities, accompanied by a satyr. Around him are members of his mythological cult, including Hercules and Ariadne. The story goes that Theseus killed the Minotaur and rescued Ariadne from the labyrinth, but on the island of Naxos he ended up leaving her, and Dionysus found her there. The composition reflects the Roman tradition of placing scenes from Greek mythology on burial monuments.To understand what Blenheim had, Heather T. Awan’s essay Roman Sarcophagi, published by the Metropolitan Museum of Art on 1 April 2007, explains how these objects came to follow the inhumation practices of the Greeks and Etruscans. The word ‘sarcophagus’ comes from the Greek for flesh-eaters; in essence, it was a stone coffin used for full-body burials. The Romans adopted this funerary practice in lieu of their earlier method of cremation. During the 2nd and 3rd centuries, it became a trend throughout the empire, which is the period Blenheim’s piece comes from.Marble was particularly prized, and the Blenheim panel is white marble. The subject of these sarcophagi consisted of mythical narratives, garlands, hunting scenes, battles and episodes from the deceased person’s life. By Awan’s account, Dionysus scenes like Blenheim’s were interpreted as a celebratory expression and emancipation from the world. In the same vein, associations between the god’s cult and a pleasurable afterlife may have also influenced their use.The Blenheim carving fits this wider artistic tradition. Its figures are derived from Greek mythology, but their placement on the burial monument gave the scene a funerary vibe. Only its front part survived, while its base was missing. The sides and back had been replaced with other stone sections, and the carved fragment functioned as a container. The History Blog records the panels as approximately 6ft long, 2 and a half feet high, and 6 inches thick, weighing around 550 pounds.From a spring basin to a palace conservation According to the History Blog, it is believed to have been acquired in the early 1800s by George Spencer-Churchill, the 5th Duke of Marlborough, Winston Churchill’s great-grandfather. However, the palace archives have no records of its arrival, or whether the duke had received it as a gift or where it came from. This much is clear: the duke was an avid collector of art and antiques.The BBC reported that the marble container was used by the duke as a water feature. It served to collect water from a natural spring near the estate’s Great Lake until it was relocated to a rock garden. This manner of using it actually had a historical precedent attached to it. It was a traditional practice of placing the ancient sarcophagi in the gardens during the 18th-century Grand Tour. In other words, when wealthy young travellers returned from Europe, they brought these classical antiquities along with them. Because of their size and shape, they were often reused as containers.After the identification, Nicolas Banfield stepped in and took charge of the object’s removal and restoration. Leading a team, they detached the marble from the lead cistern and transported it to their workshop. Describing the surviving front panel, Banfield said it was in remarkable condition given the seemingly aggressive environments it had withstood.The accumulated mineral deposits were removed by water and wooden picks while other processes involved cleaning, repair and stabilisation. It took over six months to do all this, after which it returned to Blenheim Palace. House manager Kate Bellenger welcomed its return and noted that keeping it indoors would protect it from outside elements. articles.title: Shocking murder-suicide at Pennsylvania flat: 42-year-old dad throws two children, then jumps to death
articles.summary: A 42-year-old man allegedly threw his two young children from a parking garage before jumping to his death in a suspected murder-suicide in Pennsylvania,
articles.body: A 42-year-old man allegedly threw his two young children from a parking garage before jumping to his death in a suspected murder-suicide in Pennsylvania, police said. The victims were identified as Patrick Lynch, 42, and his children, James Lynch, 8, and Caroline Lynch, 6. Their bodies were found near a parking garage in Mt Lebanon, a suburb of Pittsburgh, on Tuesday afternoon (November 3).According to preliminary findings cited in reports, Lynch allegedly pushed his two children from the upper level of the parking structure before jumping himself. All three suffered injuries consistent with a fall.Police officers, firefighters and emergency medical personnel were dispatched to the 700 block of Washington Road, near the Mt. Lebanon municipal building, at around 4:15 pm. First responders attempted to revive the three victims, but all were pronounced dead at the scene.Mt Lebanon Police chief Jason Haberman said investigators were treating the incident as a criminal investigation and not an accident."At this time we are treating this incident not as an accident," Haberman said during a news conference.The Allegheny County Police Department and the Allegheny County Sheriff's Office are assisting with the investigation. Authorities have not disclosed a possible motive.Two elementary schools closedThe deaths prompted the Mt. Lebanon School District to close Markham Elementary and Washington Elementary schools on Wednesday (November 4).In a statement, the district said it was deeply saddened by the deaths involving members of its school community. It also announced that students attending other schools could stay home, with their absences being treated as excused.Counsellors were made available to support students, teachers and families affected by the tragedy.Haberman said the incident had deeply affected the close-knit community."Everybody in the Mt. Lebanon community will know somebody involved in this incident," he said, expressing condolences to the victims' family and friends.Police said there was no active threat to the public. The investigation is ongoing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: And quiet flows the Don: Trump goes from rage to rapproachement
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent From Washington: The man who posts on social media at the drop of a hat, at all times and at odd hours, sometimes a dozen posts an hour,
articles.body: TOI Correspondent From Washington: The man who posts on social media at the drop of a hat, at all times and at odd hours, sometimes a dozen posts an hour, was rendered rather speechless after an electoral thrashing for the ages.Now a lame-duck President for all purposes but still armed with enormous executive powers, Donald Trump reacted to the Republican rout first with a mix of denial and defiance, and later with nonchalance and some conciliation. His initial reaction when the Democratic demolistion came into view early on Tuesday night was one of denial. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he posted on his propaganda platform “Truth Social.”Then it was a couple of rage posts about Fox News -- his favored propaganda network whose coverage became funereal as the night wore on -- and blaming Republican candidates, including defeated Texas Governor Greg Abbott, a wheelchair-bound GOP stalwart who was thwarted in his bid for a third term.“If Greg Abbott hadn’t become a RINO (Republican in Name Only) in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost. He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!” he wrote, throwing the veteran under the bus and absolving himself of all blame. He told Fox News that some voters simply “didn’t like the candidates.”Shortly after midnight, he posted a photo of a red baseball cap with the word VETO on it – suggesting that he will simply block any Democrat-written bills, creating a deadlock since Dems do not have the 2/3rds majority in both chambers to override a presidential veto.Then he went silent for more than nine hours, but not before he also told a C-Span in a live phone call that he would work with Democrats and not veto everything they sent, even though he has the right to do so."We're going to work with the Democrats, to make sure things go well for our country... We have a lot of friends in the Democratic Party,” he said in a conciliatory tone at odds with his familiar combativeness.Democrats too have every reason to work with the President. The U.S Constitution (Article I, Section 7) requires a two-thirds majority vote in both the House of Representatives (290/435) and the Senate (67/100) to overcome the veto – although the qualifier is 2/3rds majority of those “present and voting." Dems are well short of that double which last occurred in 1965 during the Lyndon Johnson Presidency.But a testing time is afoot even within the Republican ranks. The rout shocked and angered many conservatives, some of whom began to turn on Trump publicly. “Dems look like they might get 56 (Senate seats).. Rs will never get that back for a long time. You ignore primaries for years, anoint a charlatan as not just leader but God, and then mimic his retardation every day for a decade, at some point the chickens come home to roost,” raged Daniel Horowitz, a commentator at the right leaning outlet The Blaze. "It's on him. It's not on anybody else. It's a total, complete rejection of President Trump," Bill Miller, a top Republican lobbyist in Texas, told BBC, calling it “a disaster of the first magnitude” that nobody saw coming.Actually, every poll and survey other than MAGA affiliated ones saw it coming, although the scale was not foreseen by most. In fact, Democrats went to polling day wary of the “too good to be true” projections given past setbacks, particularly in 2016 when Trump himself did not appear to believe he would win. This time around, he tried to conjure up victory in the face of imminent defeat with bravado and bluster, but voters had other ideas. They trussed him up by giving Democrats a comfortable majority in both chambers of Congress.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney soon to become neighbors of Harry-Meghan, Beckhams? Actor views property in Cotswolds village
articles.summary: Hollywood actress Sydney Sweeney is reportedly considering a move to the English countryside after viewing a property in the picturesque Cotswolds village
articles.body: Hollywood actress Sydney Sweeney is reportedly considering a move to the English countryside after viewing a property in the picturesque Cotswolds village of Little Tew. The move could put the Euphoria and The White Lotus star among several high-profile neighbors, including Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, David and Victoria Beckham, and Ellen DeGeneres.The 29-year-old actress is reportedly planning to split her time equally between the UK and the US. She is understood to be considering the move with her boyfriend, businessman Scooter Braun, 45.According to a report by The Sun, Sweeney has visited the Cotswolds twice in the past 10 months and viewed a property in the area within the last three months. A source told the publication that the actress loves the region and finds its village lifestyle appealing."She doesn’t get bothered by locals, who are all well-used to seeing A-listers, and finds village life incredibly cute and quaint," the source said.The insider added that the English countryside would offer her a more peaceful lifestyle compared with Los Angeles."It's also a huge change of pace from LA and all the vultures circling. And she can lead a more peaceful life in the countryside," the source said.Why the Cotswolds?The Cotswolds, known for its rolling hills, honey-colored stone buildings and picturesque villages, has become a popular residential destination for celebrities.If Sweeney goes ahead with the move, she could find herself living close to Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, David and Victoria Beckham, television presenter Claudia Winkleman, singer James Blunt, Jeremy Clarkson, and Ellen DeGeneres and her wife Portia de Rossi.The location could also prove convenient for her professional commitments. Pinewood Studios, where major film productions are based, is about an hour away from the area.Sydney Sweeney's connection with the UKThe actress has visited the Cotswolds before. Last Christmas, she shared photographs from a countryside holiday, during which she stayed at the celebrity-favourite Soho Farmhouse and tried horse riding.She has also recently been in the UK filming the movie adaptation of Edith Wharton's 1913 novel The Custom of the Country, alongside her The White Lotus co-star Leo Woodall. During the visit, she was spotted wing-walking on a biplane near Ashford in Kent.Sweeney is understood to have met Braun at Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' wedding to Lauren Sanchez in June 2025.Locals have no problem with another celebrity living with themResidents in the area have reportedly welcomed the possibility of the Hollywood actress becoming their neighbour."Who doesn’t love seeing a famous person in the village? I think it would be great if the move goes ahead. She seems like a lovely woman," one local told The Sun. Another resident said the actress would feel at home given the number of celebrities already living in the region.The Cotswolds covers nearly 800 square miles across parts of Oxfordshire, Wiltshire, Warwickshire and Gloucestershire.The region has also attracted growing interest from overseas property buyers. According to a recent Savills report cited by The Sun, international buyers accounted for just over a fifth of property sales worth £1.5 million or more in the Cotswolds last year, compared with an average of 12% over the previous five years. articles.title: Tiger hit fatally by train, dragged 50m near Sengottai
articles.summary: Tiger killed after Palakkad–Thoothukudi Palaruvi Express hit it near Sengottai at 2.30am; dragged 50m. Forest officials probe movement from KMTR buffer.
articles.body: Madurai: A tiger was killed after being hit by an express train near Sengottai in the wee hours of Wednesday. The animal was struck from the side by the Palakkad–Thoothukudi Palaruvi Express and dragged about 50 metres along the tracks, preliminary postmortem findings suggest.The collision occurred around 2.30 am near Poolangudiyiruppu, between Sengottai and Bhagavathipuram railway stations in Tenkasi district. Inquiries indicated that the tiger emerged from a mango grove adjoining farmland and a residential area and was attempting to cross the tracks when the train hit it.The animal suffered a severe skull injury that caused fatal brain damage, while the rest of its body had only minor scratches, forest department sources told TOI. “No fractures were detected elsewhere, suggesting the train did not strike it head-on,” said a senior official.The animal was suspected to have come from the buffer zone of Kalakad–Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), but its identity and movements remain unconfirmed. Officials said it had not appeared in any of the camera-trap records examined so far. The site is about one kilometre outside the forest boundary. Forest officials said wildlife movement beyond the forest was difficult to predict, particularly at night.The postmortem also indicated that the tiger had eaten prey before the accident. However, officials have yet to establish why it ventured towards the grove or whether it was returning to the forest. Railway personnel alerted the authorities after the collision. Tenkasi district forest officer Rajmohan and other forest and railway officials inspected the site. Veterinarians conducted a postmortem, after which the carcass was cremated in a forest area.The incident occurred in the wider Sengottai–Aryankavu landscape, where transport routes intersect wildlife habitat. A Wildlife Institute of India assessment in 2025 identified road and rail traffic near Aryankavu as barriers to tiger movement. In June, the Palaruvi Express was stopped for an elephant crossing the tracks on another section of the route.Forest officials are installing additional cameras to monitor animal movement near the collision site. articles.title: ‘Looking for exchange of best practices’, Karnataka govt urges private schools to play mentor
articles.summary: Karnataka govt urges private schools to mentor 5,000 govt schools, sharing best practices to boost learning, retention and CET/NEET/CUET results.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Karnataka govt has urged private schools to enter into a mentor-mentee relationship with govt institutions to help them perform better.At a meeting called at Vidhana Soudha Wednesday to discuss possibilities of how private schools can help public institutions, the school education department called “for an exchange of best practices”.Rashmi V Mahesh, additional chief secretary, department of school education and literacy, said: “We are looking for a mutual exchange of best practices. Whatever track record and experience you have, share it with us.”The proposal is to mentor around 5,000 govt schools, with 200-plus enrolment, 330 Karnataka Public Schools and 590 PM Shri schools. In the first year, 1,000 schools are being targeted. Rashmi Mahesh said 34,000 science students pass every year from PU, but only 14,000 make it to CET or other competitive exams. Can private institutions help govt schools in training for these exams?While govt schools have libraries and books, there is no instructor to help the child. Similarly with sports: there are grounds, but not enough sports teachers. Govt schools are also looking for guidance on training for competitive exams. With the multigrade system giving way to monograde, govt schools are also reeling under teacher shortage, she said.“Ultimately, we are looking for better learning, attendance and retention. Additionally, we also hope to have better results in competitive exams like CET, NEET and CUET and an increase in enrolment in the mentee schools,” she added.Chief minister DK Shivakumar admitted to poor quality of govt schools. “I am not generalising, but only 50% of teachers have commitment. This, despite paying them Rs 1-lakh salary. There is a shortage of over 40,000 teachers in govt schools,” he said.“Private schools have brought recognition to Karnataka. The quality of education and capabilities of their students are commendable. If even a part of these strengths can be extended to govt schools, it will help prevent students from rural areas from migrating to cities in search of quality education,” he pointed out.“I know the economics of schools. Providing four teachers will not be a problem for you. What was the situation 10 years back? There was agreement between me and the managements that I protect you and you stand with govt. There is also a pressure to control the fee structure,” he said.In coming years, govt will put more pressure on those getting free water, power and land in the state to support govt schools. “Your basic motto should be bringing rural govt school children to the level of your school children,” he told private institutions.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news.
